I'm surprised that your mom is a doctor and doesn't seem to know very much about antidepresants and weight gain. The pills themselves won't make you gain weight, but they can alter the chemicals in your brain that make you feel satiated. This means that you may be more inclined to eat bigger portions or snack more than if you weren't taking the antidepressants. Not every antidepressant has this side-effect, and not every person will react the same way to the ones that do, but this is the reason people gain weight on antidepressants. If you're at all concerned about it, tracking your calories and exercising will help prevent it.
